function.name: %tool.listConnections.name
function.description: Lists the database connections configured in Chromite: id, name, folder, driver, connection type, production flag, read-only flag, color, connected state. Use the id or name as the 'connection' argument of other tools.

parameter.name: filter
parameter.description: Optional text to match in name, driver or folder

function.name: %tool.getConnectionInfo.name
function.description: Details of one connection without secrets: host, port, database, user name, connection type, network handlers, auto-commit default, server product and version.

parameter.name: connection
parameter.description: Connection id or name (listConnections); default: the chat's current connection

function.name: %tool.connect.name
function.description: Opens the connection if it is not open and returns its details. Other tools connect on demand too.

function.name: %tool.disconnect.name
function.description: Closes the connection for the whole application (query windows too). Uncommitted transactions make the user choose commit, roll back or cancel first.

function.name: %tool.testConnection.name
function.description: Connects and measures a round trip; returns the server product and version.

function.name: %tool.getCurrentDatabase.name
function.description: The current database and schema of the agent's session and of the connection's main session.

function.name: %tool.setCurrentDatabase.name
function.description: Sets the database and/or schema the agent's later calls on this connection use (the user's windows do not change). Most tools also take a 'database' argument for one call.

parameter.name: database
parameter.description: Database (catalog) name; empty for the connection default

function.name: %tool.getServerInfo.name
function.description: Server product, version, edition, uptime, host facts and key settings. Call it first: the version decides which system views exist. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.probePermissions.name
function.description: Which system views, permissions and extensions this login has (VIEW SERVER STATE, pg_monitor, PROCESS, V$ access, pg_stat_statements, ...) and which tools are limited without them. Call it before a health check or diagnosis.

function.name: %tool.getTransactionStatus.name
function.description: Whether the agent has an uncommitted transaction on the connection (manual-commit connections), and whether query windows have one.

function.name: %tool.commitTransaction.name
function.description: Commits the agent's open transaction on the connection. The user always confirms (commit, roll back or cancel). Call it only when the user asked to keep the changes.

function.name: %tool.rollbackTransaction.name
function.description: Rolls back the agent's open transaction on the connection. The user always confirms.

function.name: %tool.getToolPolicy.name
function.description: The user's permission for every tool on a connection: AUTO (runs), CONFIRM (asks the user), BLOCKED or READ_ONLY, with the reason. Plan around blocked tools instead of calling them.

parameter.name: connection
parameter.description: Connection id or name (empty: rules without a connection)

function.name: %tool.listDatabases.name
function.description: Databases (catalogs) of the server and the current one.

function.name: %tool.listSchemas.name
function.description: Schemas of a database and the current schema. (MySQL/MariaDB have databases instead of schemas.)

function.name: %tool.listTables.name
function.description: Tables and views of a schema (MySQL: database) with their type and comment.

function.name: %tool.describeTable.name
function.description: Columns (type, size, nullable, default, identity, comment), primary key, indexes, foreign keys and the foreign keys of other tables that reference it.

parameter.name: table
parameter.description: Table or view: name, schema.name or database.schema.name

function.name: %tool.listIndexes.name
function.description: Indexes of a table: name, unique, ordered key columns, filter.

function.name: %tool.listForeignKeys.name
function.description: Foreign keys of a table (outgoing) and of other tables pointing to it (incoming), with columns and rules.

function.name: %tool.listRoutines.name
function.description: Procedures and functions of a schema (MySQL: database).

function.name: %tool.getRoutineSource.name
function.description: Source of a procedure, function, trigger or view with LINE NUMBERS (cite them), plus parameters and properties. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

parameter.name: name
parameter.description: Routine, trigger or view: name or schema.name

function.name: %tool.listTriggers.name
function.description: Triggers of a table or a schema: timing, events, enabled. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.listSequences.name
function.description: Sequences with current value, increment and limits. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.listPrincipals.name
function.description: Logins, users, roles and role memberships. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.listPermissions.name
function.description: Granted and denied permissions on an object or of a principal. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.getObjectDdl.name
function.description: CREATE DDL of a table, view, routine or other object as Chromite generates it for the database.

function.name: %tool.getObjectDependencies.name
function.description: Dependency graph of an object: what it uses (tables, views, routines, foreign keys) and what uses it (views, routines, triggers), as nodes and edges. depth follows 'uses' edges. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.searchObjects.name
function.description: Finds tables, views, routines (and columns when asked) whose name contains a text, in all schemas of the current database.

parameter.name: types
parameter.description: Comma-separated: table, view, routine, column (default: tables, views, routines)

function.name: %tool.runSelect.name
function.description: Runs one provably read-only SELECT in a read-only transaction and returns one page of rows (offset/limit). Statements that might change data are refused: use runSql for them.

parameter.name: offset
parameter.description: Rows to skip (default 0); use nextOffset of the previous page

parameter.name: format
parameter.description: objects (default) or arrays (columns + row arrays, smaller)

function.name: %tool.runReadOnlySql.name
function.description: Runs diagnostic SQL you write (system views, SHOW, read-only DBCC and sp_who/sp_help* procedures) in a read-only, rolled-back transaction; returns every result set and server message. Anything not provably read-only is refused (use runSql).

function.name: %tool.runSql.name
function.description: Runs any single statement (DML, DDL, EXEC). The user sees the SQL and confirms unless their policy allows it; DROP/TRUNCATE/unbounded DELETE or UPDATE are DANGEROUS. On manual-commit connections the transaction stays open (transactionOpen) until commitTransaction/rollbackTransaction.

parameter.name: limit
parameter.description: Rows returned if it produces results (default 100)

function.name: %tool.runScript.name
function.description: Runs a script of several statements split by the database's delimiter rules (GO for SQL Server). Same confirmation and transaction rules as runSql; use it to apply a routine rewrite.

parameter.name: stopOnError
parameter.description: Stop at the first error (default true)

function.name: %tool.cancelQuery.name
function.description: Cancels the statements the agent is running on the connection.

function.name: %tool.explainQuery.name
function.description: Estimated execution plan without running the statement, as structured JSON: operator tree (op, object, estRows, cost, predicates), hotspots, findings (scans, key lookups, implicit conversions, missing statistics, missing indexes, compiled parameter values). SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle; others via the driver planner.

function.name: %tool.getActualPlan.name
function.description: Runs the statement and returns the actual plan with run-time values (actual rows, executions, time, reads/buffers, spills) and SET STATISTICS IO/TIME messages. Read-only statements run in a read-only transaction; others become WRITE, are confirmed by the user and rolled back. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB.

function.name: %tool.comparePlans.name
function.description: Plans of two statements (for example a query and its rewrite) side by side with a diff: cost change, operators only in A or B, actual time when actual=true (read-only statements only).

parameter.name: actual
parameter.description: Run both for actual plans (default false)

function.name: %tool.validateSql.name
function.description: Parses a statement and checks it on the server without running it (SQL Server SET NOEXEC, PostgreSQL/MySQL EXPLAIN): syntax and name errors, statement type, read-only or not, permission class.

parameter.name: server
parameter.description: Also check on the server (default true)

function.name: %tool.formatSql.name
function.description: Formats SQL with Chromite's formatter and the connection's dialect.

function.name: %tool.getQueryHistory.name
function.description: Statements the user ran in Chromite's query windows, newest first, with time, duration, rows and errors.

function.name: %tool.sampleRows.name
function.description: Rows of a table with an optional WHERE and ORDER BY (read-only).

parameter.name: orderBy
parameter.description: Order without the ORDER BY keyword

function.name: %tool.countRows.name
function.description: Exact row count of a table, optionally with a WHERE condition (scans the table; getTableStatistics gives estimates cheaply).

function.name: %tool.profileColumns.name
function.description: Per column: total and non-null rows, distinct values, min, max and the most frequent values. Scans the table once per column (max 30 columns).

parameter.name: topN
parameter.description: Most frequent values per column (default 5, 0 for none)

function.name: %tool.compareQueryResults.name
function.description: Runs two read-only queries (on the same or another connection) and compares the rows: by key columns, or as whole rows. Returns counts and samples of rows only in A, only in B and different.

parameter.name: keyColumns
parameter.description: Comma-separated key columns (default: compare whole rows)

function.name: %tool.insertRows.name
function.description: Inserts rows into a table; values are converted to the column types. One call is one transaction on auto-commit connections.

function.name: %tool.updateRows.name
function.description: Updates rows identified by a key that covers the primary key or a unique index (other keys are refused).

parameter.name: key
parameter.description: JSON object {keyColumn: value} or a JSON array of them

function.name: %tool.deleteRows.name
function.description: Deletes rows identified by a key that covers the primary key or a unique index (other keys are refused).

parameter.name: key
parameter.description: JSON object {keyColumn: value} or a JSON array of them

function.name: %tool.generateDdl.name
function.description: Builds the DDL of a change without running it, with the same arguments as the matching DDL tool (operation: createTable, alterTable, dropTable, createView, dropView, createIndex, dropIndex). Show it to the user before changing anything.

parameter.name: columns
parameter.description: createTable: JSON array of {name, type, nullable, default, identity}; createIndex: comma-separated columns with optional ASC/DESC

parameter.name: default
parameter.description: alterTable addColumn: default value or expression

parameter.name: include
parameter.description: createIndex: comma-separated INCLUDE columns (SQL Server, PostgreSQL)

function.name: %tool.createTable.name
function.description: Creates a table from column definitions; the user sees the DDL and confirms.

parameter.name: columns
parameter.description: JSON array of {name, type, nullable, default, identity}

function.name: %tool.alterTable.name
function.description: Adds, drops or renames a column, or changes its type; the user sees the DDL and confirms.

function.name: %tool.dropTable.name
function.description: Drops a table and its data. DANGEROUS: the user confirms.

function.name: %tool.createView.name
function.description: Creates (or with replace=true replaces) a view from a read-only SELECT.

function.name: %tool.dropView.name
function.description: Drops a view. DANGEROUS: the user confirms.

function.name: %tool.createIndex.name
function.description: Creates an index (optionally unique, with INCLUDE columns on SQL Server/PostgreSQL); the user sees the DDL and confirms.

parameter.name: columns
parameter.description: Comma-separated key columns, each optionally ASC or DESC

function.name: %tool.dropIndex.name
function.description: Drops an index; the user sees the DDL and confirms.

function.name: %tool.exportData.name
function.description: Exports the rows of a read-only query or a table to a CSV, JSON or XLSX file on this computer (max 1,000,000 rows; default 100,000).

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Absolute path of the file to write

function.name: %tool.importCsv.name
function.description: Inserts the rows of a CSV file (header = column names) into an existing table of 'connection'. One transaction on auto-commit connections.

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Absolute path of the CSV file

function.name: %tool.copyTable.name
function.description: Copies the rows of a table from sourceConnection (default: the same) into a table of 'connection', optionally creating the target table. For large or type-sensitive copies, suggest the Data Transfer wizard instead.

parameter.name: createTarget
parameter.description: Create the target table from the source columns (default false)

function.name: %tool.listSessions.name
function.description: User sessions with login, host, program, status, current wait and statement. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

parameter.name: activeOnly
parameter.description: Only sessions running something or holding a transaction

function.name: %tool.getBlockingChain.name
function.description: Who blocks whom right now as a tree: head blockers (login, host, program, transaction age, isolation, open transactions, last SQL), waiters (wait type, time, resource, SQL), their locks mapped to objects and indexes, and rule-based findings and fix suggestions. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

parameter.name: database
parameter.description: Database whose objects the locks are mapped to; default: current

function.name: %tool.listLocks.name
function.description: Held and waited locks grouped by session, object, index and mode, a summary, and lock escalation counters (SQL Server). SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

parameter.name: database
parameter.description: Database whose objects the locks are mapped to

function.name: %tool.getDeadlocks.name
function.description: Recent deadlocks: SQL Server system_health deadlock graphs as JSON (victims, processes with SQL and stack, resources with owners and waiters); MySQL/MariaDB the latest InnoDB deadlock; PostgreSQL the counters.

function.name: %tool.listOpenTransactions.name
function.description: Transactions open longer than minSeconds, including idle-in-transaction sessions, with age, locks and last SQL. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.getLongRunningQueries.name
function.description: Requests running longer than minSeconds with CPU, reads, waits and blocking. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.killSession.name
function.description: Ends a server session; its open transaction is rolled back. DANGEROUS and a last resort: the user confirms (and is told when the session has an open transaction).

function.name: %tool.getWaitStats.name
function.description: What the server waits on: cumulative waits without benign ones (SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle) or current session waits (PostgreSQL).

function.name: %tool.getTopQueries.name
function.description: Most expensive statements: SQL Server plan cache, PostgreSQL pg_stat_statements, MySQL performance_schema digests, Oracle V$SQL.

function.name: %tool.getDatabaseSizes.name
function.description: Size of every database (data and log). SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.getSpaceUsage.name
function.description: Data and log files with used and free space, log usage and its reuse wait, disk volumes (SQL Server); tablespaces, largest tables, WAL (PostgreSQL); schemas and largest tables (MySQL); tablespace usage (Oracle).

function.name: %tool.getBackupHistory.name
function.description: Last full/differential/log backup per database with age and warnings, and recent backups (SQL Server msdb); WAL archiving (PostgreSQL); RMAN jobs (Oracle).

function.name: %tool.getJobHistory.name
function.description: Recent job runs, failures by default: SQL Server Agent (msdb), pg_cron, MySQL events, Oracle scheduler.

parameter.name: failedOnly
parameter.description: Only failed or canceled runs (default true)

function.name: %tool.getErrorLog.name
function.description: Recent server log entries, optionally only those containing a text: SQL Server error log, PostgreSQL current log file, MySQL 8 error_log table, Oracle alert log.

parameter.name: contains
parameter.description: Text the entry contains (for example deadlock, error, failed)

function.name: %tool.getServerConfig.name
function.description: Key server and database settings with sanity findings (MAXDOP, cost threshold, memory, auto shrink, shared_buffers, work_mem, autovacuum, buffer pool, ...).

function.name: %tool.backupDatabase.name
function.description: SQL Server: BACKUP DATABASE/LOG to a file on the server (copy-only and checksum by default, so the backup chain is not changed). The user sees the T-SQL and confirms.

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Backup file path on the server

function.name: %tool.restoreDatabase.name
function.description: SQL Server: restores a database from a backup file on the server (the latest full backup set and the sets after it), moving files to the server's default folders. DANGEROUS: the user sees the T-SQL and confirms.

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Backup file path on the server

function.name: %tool.getTableStatistics.name
function.description: Row counts, table and index sizes, statistics last update, rows sampled, modifications since the update, dead rows and vacuum/analyze times. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle.

function.name: %tool.getIndexUsage.name
function.description: How indexes are used since the server started: seeks, scans, lookups, updates, key and included columns, lock escalations. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL (performance_schema), Oracle (statistics only).

function.name: %tool.getMissingIndexes.name
function.description: Missing-index suggestions of the SQL Server optimizer with a suggested CREATE INDEX; PostgreSQL: large tables read mostly by sequential scans.

function.name: %tool.getUnusedIndexes.name
function.description: Indexes that are written but never read since the last restart, and duplicate or left-prefix indexes. SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB.

function.name: %tool.getIndexFragmentation.name
function.description: Fragmentation with REBUILD/REORGANIZE suggestions (SQL Server), dead rows and leaf density (PostgreSQL, pgstattuple if installed), reclaimable space (MySQL).

function.name: %tool.getRoutineStats.name
function.description: Run-time statistics of a procedure, function or trigger and of each statement inside it with its start line (SQL Server); function statistics and nested statements (PostgreSQL); program statistics (MySQL).

function.name: %tool.getCachedPlans.name
function.description: SQL Server: cached plans per statement of a routine (by start line) or of statements containing a text, parsed like explainQuery (operators, warnings, compiled parameter values).

function.name: %tool.listLibraryQueries.name
function.description: Saved queries of the Chromite Query Library: id, name, description, folder, target connection, parameters, thresholds.

parameter.name: contains
parameter.description: Text in name, description or SQL

function.name: %tool.getLibraryQuery.name
function.description: One library query with its SQL, parameters and thresholds.

function.name: %tool.runLibraryQuery.name
function.description: Runs a library query with parameters (bound, not concatenated) on its target or the given connection and judges the result against its thresholds. Queries that may change data become WRITE and need 'connection'.

function.name: %tool.runMonitoringChecks.name
function.description: Runs every read-only query of a library folder and judges each against its @threshold entries: OK, WARN, CRITICAL, NO_THRESHOLDS, SKIPPED, ERROR, plus a summary.

function.name: %tool.openInEditor.name
function.description: Opens SQL in a new query window of the Chromite app for the user (does not run it).
